summary: Five substantial cuts toward the Phase 5e recovery ceremony, stopping at a clean checkpoint before the initiator side (5e-v) + locked-screen wiring + combine + recovery-succession event (5e-vii). The math is proven end-to-end and the responder half of the ceremony is fully implemented. Cut 1 (8ea9393): storage migration to v2 with K_data reuse — the load-bearing K_data-stable property across saves. Cut 2 (806c45e): recovery-share builders — createShares.ts with NIP-44 wrap-to-peer. Cut 3 (71c9dc6): distribute + receive routing — DistributeSharesModal + inbox routing. Cut 4 (commit between 71c9dc6 and 1b089a5): envelope helpers for both ceremony directions plus an end-to-end round-trip test that walks the full ceremony in-process (operator encrypts blob, extracts K_data, builds shares, peers hold them, OPERATOR'S KEYPAIR IS FORGOTTEN, new ceremony Wallet builds recovery-request, three of five peers respond, ceremony combines and decryptRecoverableWithKData decrypts the original plaintext back). Cut 5 (1b089a5): RecoveryResponderModal — strict out-of-band verification gating per brief decision 5; finds held share matching subject + share_for; builds + sends share-response via existing transport. D-03 stays loud across all five cuts.

outcome.notes: [P-001] Storage migration is backwards-compatible; K_data stays stable across saves so distributed shares stay valid forever. [P-002] The end-to-end round-trip test in createRecoveryRequest.test.ts walks the full ceremony in-process — proves the math half before any UI ships. [P-003] Responder modal is fully shipped with strict out-of-band verification gating. [P-004] Initiator side (5e-v), locked-screen wiring, combine + restore, and recovery-succession event (5e-vii) remain for the fresh session. [P-005] The latent threshold-leaf bug in createCohort.readCohort (numeric leaf read via leafValue returns 0; default-fallback masks it) is still flagged as a small follow-on cut. [FEEDBACK→Foreman]: the initiator side requires ephemeral NostrTransport for the ceremony keypair (which has no Supabase session) — the cleanest architecture is to instantiate NostrTransport with the ceremony Wallet's keypair and current relays from prefs, live for the duration of the modal. Worth pre-noting in the brief or as a doctrine decision before the next session cuts the locked-screen wiring.

uncertainty: All five cuts are tested via unit tests and the end-to-end ceremony round-trip is proven in-process. The UI choreography of the responder modal is browser-untested; the strict verification gating language deserves a real-device walk before the ceremony first runs in anger. The bigger uncertainty is the initiator side: the ephemeral transport question, the locked-screen entry point, the combine + restore + succession choreography — all multi-round protocol-state-machine work for the next session.

next: Initiator side. Phase 5e-v + locked-screen wiring + combine + 5e-vii recovery-succession event. The initiator generates a ceremony Wallet on the new device, instantiates an ephemeral NostrTransport tied to the ceremony pubkey, lets the operator enter their old identity pubkey plus cohort member pubkeys (because the new device has no local cohort credential), sends recovery-request envelopes to each, listens for share-response envelopes on the ceremony pubkey's subscription, combines M responses via combineShares once they arrive, decrypts the cloud blob via Wallet.restoreFromKData, builds a recovery-succession meta-kind attestation, and walks M peers through co-signing it. On success, the operator picks a new passphrase and the restored wallet saves under v2 with a fresh K_data. The lock-screen entry point in UnlockPrompt adds a 'Lost passphrase? Start recovery' link that opens RecoveryInitiatorModal.
